source: McCoy, Yao, Friedman, Hardy, Griffiths (2024) When a language model is optimized for reasoning, does it still show embers of autoregression? OpenAI o1
finding: o1-preview beats earlier LLMs, especially on rare task variants, but still does better on high-probability outputs. Output-probability sensitivity persists in a reasoning model.
numbers: Shift cipher: o1 accuracy 47% (lowest-probability outputs) to 92% (highest). Acronyms: 100% common vs 99.9% rare variant, yet far more thinking tokens on the rare variant. Harder sorting (all words start with i): o1 better on alphabetical than reverse. Earlier LLMs (GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Claude 3, Llama 3, Gemini 1.0) showed large common-vs-rare gaps; o1 mostly did not on accuracy.
quote: o1 ... still displays the same qualitative trends that we observed in previous systems.
limits: Only a subset of tasks (o1 is costly); o1-preview Sept 2024; ceiling effects hide task-frequency effects; thinking-token counts are the only view into o1's reasoning.
agent_relevance: Gap 1 and 7: reasoning training shrinks but does not remove the statistical-prior effect. Expect worse accuracy on low-probability or rare-variant inputs; thinking-token spend can serve as a difficulty signal.

source: Wu et al. (2024) Reasoning or Reciting? Counterfactual tasks
finding: Across 11 counterfactual task pairs (base-9 arithmetic, shifted code indexing, rotated spatial frames, altered chess rules, drop-D guitar and others), GPT-4, GPT-3.5, Claude and PaLM-2 do above chance but much worse than on default tasks. Default and counterfactual accuracy are positively correlated.
numbers: GPT-4 two-digit addition, first column group of the table: base-10 100.0 vs base-9 23.4 (1,000 instances); a third column group (200 instances, header not checked) shows base-9 at 90.0. GPT-3.5 parseable programs fell from 99% default to 62% counterfactual. In arithmetic, base-10 accuracy decays much more slowly with digit count than other bases (memorisation sign). 0-shot CoT helps in most cases but hurts some default tasks (GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 chord fingering; PaLM-2 base-10 and 16 addition).
limits: GPT-4-0314 era; reasoning models not tested. Authors say it is a continuum, not reasoning versus reciting. Table column headers were hard to read from the pdf text.
agent_relevance: Gap 7: drop is real but partial. Treat accuracy on the familiar variant as an upper bound; test the scaffold on a counterfactual twin of each task.

source: Mirzadeh et al. (2025) GSM-Symbolic: limits of mathematical reasoning in LLMs (ICLR 2025)
finding: Re-instantiating GSM8K templates with new names and numbers lowers accuracy and raises variance. Changing only names barely matters; changing numbers matters more; adding one irrelevant clause (GSM-NoOp) causes large drops, including for o1-preview.
numbers: GSM-NoOp: Phi-3-mini fell by more than 65%; o1-preview also showed significant declines (exact figure not extracted). Accuracy falls and variance rises as clauses are added (P1, P2 variants). GPT-4o and Llama3-8b show a negligible drop from GSM8K to GSM-Symbolic; Gemma2-9B, Phi-3, Mathstral-7B drop more.
limits: Mid-2024 models; contamination is one proposed cause, pattern matching another. The 'no genuine logical reasoning' reading is the authors' interpretation.
agent_relevance: Gap 7: perturbations of names, numbers and irrelevant clauses cut accuracy even in o1. Add an irrelevant-clause probe to the G-type checks.

source: Shojaee et al. (2025) The Illusion of Thinking: reasoning models via problem complexity (Apple)
finding: On four controllable puzzles (Tower of Hanoi, Checker Jumping, River Crossing, Blocks World), reasoning models (o3-mini, DeepSeek-R1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet thinking) collapse to near-zero accuracy beyond a model-specific compositional depth, while reducing thinking tokens near the collapse point. Giving the solution algorithm does not move the collapse point.
numbers: Three regimes at equal inference compute: low complexity, non-thinking models beat thinking ones; medium, thinking wins; high, both collapse. Hanoi with 10 disks needs 1,023 moves; models fail at about move 100 (N=10); in River Crossing the first error comes by move 4. With the algorithm in the prompt, failure still occurs at roughly the same complexity.
limits: Puzzle tasks only; 64k token budget for Claude 3.7; later commentary on token limits and puzzle solvability not read this session. Paper version 3 dated Nov 2025.
agent_relevance: Gap 1: productivity (longer compositions) still fails in current reasoning models; long exact procedures should go to code or tools, not longer thinking.

source: Sprague et al. (2025) To CoT or not to CoT? Chain-of-thought helps mainly on math and symbolic reasoning (ICLR 2025)
finding: Meta-analysis of over 100 papers plus 20 datasets by 14 models: CoT helps mainly on math, symbolic and logic tasks. Splitting plan from execution shows CoT mostly helps execution, and a plan plus symbolic solver or Python tool beats CoT for both steps.
numbers: Mean CoT gains in the literature: symbolic +14.2, math +12.3, logic +6.9 points. Other categories 56.8 with CoT vs 56.1 without. On MMLU about 95% of the gain comes from questions with an equals sign in question or output. Individual-model gains up to 66.9% (GSM8K) and 41.6% (MATH). Plan + Tool solver (PAL for GSM8K) dominated Plan + CoT solver in most settings.
quote: CoT ... underperforms relative to using a symbolic solver.
limits: Models up to Llama 3.1 and GPT-4o; reasoning-trained models only partly covered. Not a head-to-head of PAL against CoT at equal tokens on every task.
agent_relevance: Gap 5: code-as-thought still beats CoT where the task is symbolic; on soft reasoning neither helps much. Route symbolic steps to code; skip CoT on soft tasks to save tokens.

source: Wang and Sun (2026) Is the Reversal Curse a Binding Problem? (ICLR 2026)
finding: Authors argue the Reversal Curse comes from inconsistent and entangled concept representations (a binding failure). A JEPA-style model breaks the curse without data augmentation; memory layers that keep concepts disentangled help further.
numbers: Standard transformers trained with surface-level next-token prediction scored 0.0% on reversal regardless of depth or tied embeddings. JEPA-based design generalises to reversal (exact figures not extracted).
limits: Small models trained from scratch on synthetic relations, not frontier LLMs. Does not test Claude, GPT-5 or reasoning models.
agent_relevance: Gap 3 and 10: the fix is architectural, not prompt-level. A memory store that writes both A-to-B and B-to-A facts at write time sidesteps the curse; untested here.

source: Search summary: arXiv 2411.16353, nine frontier LLMs on two-hop reasoning without CoT
finding: A search-result summary says nine frontier LLMs completely fail two-hop no-CoT reasoning in over half of real-world question categories. Not opened.
agent_relevance: Gap 1 and 3: a lead for the next pass; do not cite numbers.

source: Yang, Campbell, Huang, Wang, Cohen, Webb (2025) Emergent symbolic mechanisms support abstract reasoning in LLMs
finding: Mechanistic study of Llama-3.1, Qwen2.5 and Gemma-2 (more equivocal for GPT-2) finds a three-stage architecture: symbol abstraction heads turn tokens into abstract variables, symbolic induction heads run sequence induction over them, retrieval heads read out the value. Ablating these heads drives the correct-answer probability to zero while control ablations do not.
numbers: Llama-3.1 70B reaches 95% in the 2-shot rule induction task. Three tasks tested. Heads found by causal mediation; cumulative ablation sends the correct-answer probability to zero.
limits: Simple in-context abstract tasks (ABA/ABB style) in open models up to 72B. No frontier closed models, no compositional benchmarks. 'Symbolic' is the authors' interpretation.
agent_relevance: Gap 10: direct evidence of variable-binding-like circuits in LLMs. Supports a weak LoT as an emergent mechanism; background only for the scaffold.

source: Zheng et al. (2025) ProcessBench: identifying process errors in mathematical reasoning
finding: 3,400 human-annotated solutions. Many solutions with correct final answers still contain a wrong step, and the share rises with difficulty. Prompted critic models beat existing process reward models on the harder subsets; o1-mini is the best critic.
numbers: Correct-answer solutions containing a process error: GSM8K 3.5% (200-193 of 200), MATH 18.8% (500-406 of 500), OlympiadBench 32.2% (500-339), Omni-MATH 51.8% (500-241). Overall F1 in the headline figure: o1-mini 87.9, QwQ-32B-Preview 71.5, GPT-4o-0806 61.9. Math-Shepherd-PRM-7B F1 on Omni-MATH 16.9.
limits: Math only; critic prompting, not agent loops with tools; hidden-step rate of reasoning models with tools was not measured.
agent_relevance: Gap 4: hidden wrong steps persist and grow with difficulty. A step-level check should use the strongest model available, not a small verifier.

source: Hao et al. (2024, v4 2026) Training LLMs to reason in a continuous latent space (Coconut)
finding: Coconut feeds the last hidden state back as the next input. It beats CoT on search-heavy logic with fewer tokens, but loses to CoT on GSM8k math.
numbers: GSM8k: CoT 42.9%, Coconut 34.1%, no-CoT 16.5%. ProsQA: CoT 77.5%, Coconut 97.0%. ProntoQA: Coconut 99.8%, CoT 98.8%. (Table columns misaligned in the pdf text; read by hand.) Continuous thoughts can hold several next-step options, like breadth-first search.
limits: Multi-stage curriculum on GPT-2 and Llama models; ProsQA is the authors' own dataset. No independent replication found this session.
agent_relevance: Gap 9: not replicated here. A prompt-level analogue would be keeping several candidate plans alive before committing; nothing here tests that in a prompt.

source: Rabagliati, Ferguson, Lew-Williams (2019) The profile of abstract rule learning in infancy: meta-analytic and experimental evidence
finding: Meta-analysis of infant abstract repetition-rule learning (ABB, AAB) finds a small-to-medium average effect that varies with stimulus meaning. Infants learn rules mostly from meaningful stimuli.
numbers: 20 reports, 1,318 infants, 63 experiments (95 records). Overall Hedges g 0.25, SE 0.08, 95% CI [0.09, 0.40], p = 0.002. Authors flag likely publication bias after Marcus 2007's high-powered null on tones, note independent replications are rare, and use p-curve analysis.
limits: Heterogeneity between studies was significant. Looking-time measures are noisy. Effect is not speech-specific.
agent_relevance: Gap 6: infant evidence for rule extraction is real but small (g about 0.25) and conditional. Do not use it as proof of a rigid symbol system.

source: Marcus, Vijayan, Bandi Rao, Vishton (1999) Rule learning by seven-month-old infants
finding: Three experiments: 7-month-olds looked longer at sentences with unfamiliar structures than at familiar ones. The design ruled out counting, transitional probabilities and a popular class of simple neural networks.
numbers: Abstract read only; sample sizes and looking times not extracted. The 2019 meta-analysis puts the average effect over 63 experiments at g 0.25.
limits: Abstract only via Europe PMC. Connectionist replies and later nulls contest the strong reading.
agent_relevance: Gap 6: founding human datum for algebraic rules. Background only.

source: Marcus, Fernandes, Johnson (2007) Infant rule learning facilitated by speech
finding: Infants extract ABB rules from speech but not from tones, animal sounds or timbres unless they first hear the rule in speech.
numbers: Abstract read only; numbers not extracted. The 2019 meta-analysis calls this a high-powered null on tones.
limits: Abstract only. Later work (Ferguson and Lew-Williams 2016, per the meta-analysis) shows non-speech learning when communicatively primed.
agent_relevance: Gap 6: boundary condition. Format and meaning cues matter, which fits tagging inputs with meaning before asking for structure.

source: Murphy, Mondragon, Murphy (2008) Rule learning by rats (Science)
finding: Rats learned that sequences consistent with a rule (XYX) differ from XXY or YXX, and transferred the rule to new stimuli.
numbers: Abstract read only; counts not extracted.
limits: Abstract only. Replication status not checked this session.
agent_relevance: Gap 6: structural rule transfer is not unique to humans; weakens a language-specific reading of the LoT argument.

source: Lake and Baroni (2023) Human-like systematic generalization through a meta-learning neural network (Nature)
finding: Abstract only (Europe PMC): meta-learning for compositionality (MLC) matches human systematicity and flexibility in a head-to-head test of seven models, and improves systematic generalization benchmarks.
numbers: No figures read; full text not retrievable this session. Earlier files record 99.78% on a SCAN-style benchmark, unchecked.
limits: No independent replication on structural splits or prompt-only version found; search budget was used up.
agent_relevance: Gap 8: stays open. No evidence that a prompt-only version reaches comparable systematicity.

source: Berglund et al. (2024) The Reversal Curse, via a search-result digest
finding: Search digest repeats the original: GPT-4 answers forward celebrity-parent questions 79% and reverse 33%; effect holds across model sizes and is not removed by augmentation; with A-is-B in the context window GPT-4 infers B-is-A.
limits: No 2025-2026 frontier-model reversal test found by the single search. In-context fix is from the digest, not re-read.
agent_relevance: Gap 3: putting both directions in context avoids the curse; a direct agent-memory test is still missing.
